title: High-Dimensional Deterministic Secure Quantum Communication with Reed-Solomon Erasure Coding
authors: L. F. A. de Sousa Moura, G. L. Zanin, P. H. Souto Ribeiro, C. Becker Westphall
abstract: Deterministic Secure Quantum Communication (DSQC) is a quantum cryptographic technique engineered to transfer a message through a quantum channel, requiring an auxiliary classical channel for eavesdropping verification and decoding, but without prior key distribution. This article presents a theoretical high-dimensional prepare and measure DSQC protocol using the Reed-Solomon erasure coding to ensure data resilience to noise. This protocol offers the following benefits: it eliminates the need for quantum memory or entanglement, it can be built with commercially available technology, and its higher capacity improves the overall transmission rate.
summary: This paper proposes a novel Deterministic Secure Quantum Communication protocol that enhances data resilience by incorporating Reed-Solomon erasure coding into a high-dimensional quantum state transmission scheme. It utilizes single photons encoded in spatial degrees of freedom, eliminating the need for quantum memory or entanglement. The combination of classical error correction with quantum security measures makes the protocol highly practical and robust.
main_problem: To develop a Deterministic Secure Quantum Communication (DSQC) protocol that transmits messages over a quantum channel while ensuring resilience against noise and eavesdropping, without requiring prior key distribution, quantum memory, or entanglement.
main_result: The protocol successfully integrates Reed-Solomon erasure coding with high-dimensional quantum states encoded in the transverse spatial degrees of freedom, achieving deterministic secure transmission.
method: The method combines classical polynomial encoding (Reed-Solomon coding) with quantum state preparation and measurement in Mutually Unbiased Bases (MUB) using single photons.
model_or_system: The system uses high-dimensional quantum states encoded in the Transverse Spatial Degrees of Freedom (TSDF) of single photons, generated via Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (SPDC). Implementation relies on components like SLMs and photon counting matrices.
key_observables: Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER), error introduced by Eve (EIR), and the successfully recovered message bits.
important_parameters: Alphabet size (q or d, a prime number), message length (k), and the number of parity bits (2t).
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes the availability of an authenticated classical channel for announcing decoy positions and values, and that the total number of photons transmitted in a block satisfies n < q.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the block diagram of the RS encoding/decoding process, the experimental setup using SPDC to generate heralded single photons, and flowcharts detailing the protocol steps.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework by first establishing the need for DSQC, then presenting the combination of RS coding with high-dimensional quantum states, followed by mathematical derivations for error rates and block sizes, and concluding with a discussion of the experimental realization.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum communication security and capacity enhancement by merging classical coding theory with quantum optics, which is highly relevant to photonic quantum information processing.
